Review: I decided to give Burt's Bees Lip Balm a try after seeing it recommended by a few friends. I was looking for a natural lip balm that would moisturize my lips and keep them soft and healthy. I have to say, the Vanilla Bean flavor is quite pleasant, it has a nice scent and it goes on smoothly, but unfortunately, I found that it doesn't moisturize my lips as much as I was hoping. My lips still feel dry after applying it, and I need to apply it multiple times a day to keep them moisturized.The packaging is also quite small, so I found that I had to replace it frequently. This might be a problem for people who are always on the go and don't have time to constantly repurchase the lip balm. I also noticed that the balm gets quite soft in warm weather, which makes it difficult to apply without making a mess. This can be quite frustrating when you're out and about and don't want to mess up your bag or pockets.Another issue I had with Burt's Bees Lip Balm is that it doesn't last long enough. Even though I apply it multiple times throughout the day, I still find that my lips start feeling dry again after just a few hours. This can be quite frustrating when you're out and about and don't have time to constantly reapply the lip balm.Overall, I am a bit disappointed with Burt's Bees Lip Balm. While the natural ingredients and vanilla flavor are nice, I don't find it to be very moisturizing, and the small packaging and lack of durability are downsides. I'll probably try a different lip balm in the future. 3 stars.It's worth mentioning that my review is based on my own personal experience and preferences, other people may have different experiences with this product. Also, it's important to note that everyone's skin is different and what works for one person may not work for another.

Review Title: Worst Shopping Experience Here in 15 Years
Review: I’ve been shopping on Amazon for more than 15 years, and I’ve never had what I’d call a really bad experience until now.I ordered 4 2-packs of Burt’s Bees grapefruit lip balm. I’ve used them for a long time. The selling page, which advertises new product, shows a small, branded box for a 2-pack. That’s how they’ve always arrived when I’ve ordered them.This time, the product arrived in plastic bags (shown in photo). I didn’t think much about it until I opened the first lip balm. It tasted terrible, as in bitter with a weird chemical-like flavor. I thought maybe my taste was off, so I went and grabbed an open Burt’s Bees grapefruit lip balm from my car. It tasted fine and had a grapefruit flavor, as it should. I tried the new one again. Still nasty. I opened 2 more (of the 8 in my purchase), and they were just as bad.When I looked more closely at all 8 lip balms, I noticed that they had different names. Some said, “Pink Grapefruit Moisturizing Lip Balm”. Others said, “Refreshing Lip Balm with Pink Grapefruit” (shown in photo). On the back of the labels are batch numbers, referred to as UPC codes on the Burt’s Bees website. There were 2 matching pairs of UPC codes on the 8 I bought, but most of the codes (shown in photo) are very different. Today I went to a local store and bought 3 lip balms (in photo). They all had the same UPC code, which is to be expected.The thing that really solved this mystery for me, though, was the old, faded price sticker (shown in photo). It tells me exactly where these lip balms came from, why they tasted so terrible, and why the UPC codes are mostly different. It’s $30+ dollars I’ll never get back.

Review Title: I Really Wanted to Like It But…
Review: So I saw soooo many good reviews on this chapstick and I’ve heard even from friends this is a good brand— which it is. But it just didn’t work for me.It started off great the first week. My lips were soft and no longer chapped as they have been since moving back to the dry climate of the West Coast. But after about a week and a half I began to develop Angular Cheilitis which is when your swollen patches of skin appear on the corners of the mouths. I realized it was because of the Burt Bees. My little sister got a similar reaction and so we both stopped using it. The AC disappeared but now my lips are cracked again so it’s like, welp.I really wanted to like this product, I did. Maybe their other formulas might work better for me. But this wasn’t it.

Review Title: Warning: Please Check if You Are Allergic To This!
Review: I never knew I was allergic to certain lip-balms until I tried this.First off, each of the lip balms smelled great and had a bit of sweet flavor to it. They were pretty nice and I was really excited to use all of them. HOWEVER, ever since I started using one my lips started to swell. At first I suspected that it was caused by stress because, during that time, I was overburdened with work. Adding to that, I never had any allergic reactions to lip balms from other brands. Well, the swelling kept persisting and it took about a month before suspecting that this lip balm could be causing the swelling.I tossed one away and tried another. Swelling persisted. So I tossed that one and tried another. Review: While using this product, I slowly developed perioral dermatitis (acne like rash around my mouth that eventually traveled up my nose to my forehead). It took me almost a year to determine that this was in fact the cause of it. I saw a dermatologist twice, went on antibiotics twice and was prescribed two facial creams however my perioral dermatitis continued. It got so bad I was embarrassed to go out in public at times. I started cutting foods out of my diet thinking something I was eating was causing it. I switched to a fluoride free toothpaste and made a bunch of other life style changes. I spent hours researching online. It didn’t cross my mind that this lip balm could be causing it because I associate this brand with natural ingredients. I finally came across a website that stated that peppermint oil can cause perioral dermatitis. I stopped using this immediately and what do you know? My skin slowly starting clearing up. I went back to my normal diet and fluoride toothpaste and my skin continued clearing up. It’s almost been a couple weeks and my perioral dermatitis is nearly gone.

Review: Take a few minutes to look up limonene and eugenol, which are both listed ingredients in the original version, and possibly other versions, of BBs lip balm.From the internet search I did; Should I avoid limonene? Topically, limonene can cause sensitivity and is best avoided. Also, because of its penetration-enhancing effects on skin, it's particularly important to avoid products that contain limonene plus other skin sensitizers <clove oil>.Eugenol, or clove oil; Is eugenol toxic to humans?  Eugenol is listed by the FDA as GRAS (generally recognized as safe) when consumed orally, in unburned form. It is nontoxic in food but toxic upon inhalation. High doses of eugenol may cause damage to the liver (Thompson et al., 1998).  This stuff goes on your lips, right under your nose, and if used multiple times a day, we are breathing in toxic fumes each time. All 4 tubes went right in the trash.  What a waste of money.  Do Not Recommend.

Review Title: Not for me, doesn't hurt to try if it works for you
Review: I was using Burts Bees Pomegranate before switching to these. I tried it out for a good 5 months but I had to switch back to Burts Bees.These work 'well enough', but definitely did not reach my expectations. It feels good on the lips, it doesn't feel too oily but I guess that's the achilles heel of these. These are specifically worded as 'lip repair' not 'lip balm'. So if you intend to use these as a replacement for your current lip balm keep in mind that these may not work well for you as an everyday use. Perhaps maybe as a once a day application(?).
